newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wesfarmers shares sparkle after result.
newsitem.headline: Wesfarmers shares sparkle after result.

text.p: Shares in Wesfarmers Ltd rose further in afternoon trading on Tuesday, climbing 46 cents to A$12.55, after the company reporting a 50 percent increase in net profit to A$139.55 million for the 12 months to June 30.

Immediately prior to the announcement, shares in the agricultural, energy and hardware group were 24 cents higher on the day at A$12.33, in modest trade. The company said its upbeat performance should continue, with further growth in revenue and earnings expected in the 1997/98 financial year.

"The result was pretty much in line with analysts' forecasts but the (increased) dividend was a surprise," said a Perth-based dealer, noting the flow on effect to Wesfarmer's 51 percent shareholder, The Franked Income Fund.
"That is a generous payout which has reflected straight away on the Franked Income Fund," the dealer said.
Franked Income Fund units were nine cents higher at A$3.96 by 2.10 p.m. (0210 GMT).
Strong growth in 1997/98 would be generated from the expanding hardware warehouse chain with the expected upturn in the housing market to also lift earnings, Wesfarmers said.

The company said the outlook for the rural sector remained uncertain, although some recovery in wool and cattle prices had been factored into group budgets. The fertilisers/chemicals and gas/coal sectors were expected to continue to make strong contributions to group profits with similar results to 1996/97.
By 2.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), Wesfarmers shares were 51 cents higher at A$12.60 on turnover of 78,071 shares.
